newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Slightly down but uptrend intact.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Slightly down but uptrend intact.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market weakened slightly on Tuesday but some traders said the uptrend momentum has not yet ended.
The market has been expecting seasonal tighter supplies from the Middle East and South Korea starting the second half of May, supporting overall sentiment, traders said.
The 180-cst was heard traded between two majors at $101.00 per tonne for delivery between May 28 and June 1, compared with last week's $102.00 traded level.
Two to three Middle East cargoes committed to a local trader are expected to arrive in Singapore in the coming few days, fuelling speculations that the trader would bid up the market.
Some traders speculated that the local trader, who bought one cargo last week at $102.00 per tonne, would bid up prices to coincide with the arrival of the cargoes.
"The local trader did not emerge today but people are still waiting," said one trader.
Market focus was also on two fuel oil tenders for imports and exports, traders said.

The Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO) tendered to buy two 70,000-tonne cargoes of 0.3-percent 540-centistoke fuel oil for July delivery while Taiwan tendered to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent fuel oil for June lifting on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
In the LSWR market, bearish sentiment continued amid ample supplies in May and poor demand from Japan, traders said.
